hypotheses.claim: Physical placement should be represented by independent transaction, data, index, compute, process and fault-domain axes rather than one monolith-vs-isolated label.
hypotheses.counter: One store-level placement label is sufficient.

hypotheses.claim: Fused same-process query computation can be beneficial while vector or graph indexes remain physically decoupled.
hypotheses.counter: Compute fusion only pays when storage is also unified.

hypotheses.claim: Cross-modal query affinity should drive compute colocation more strongly than semantic unity itself.
hypotheses.counter: Semantic unity predicts physical colocation benefit.

hypotheses.claim: Vector data and ANN index metadata can require different physical placement because their write/read/compression behavior differs.
hypotheses.counter: Index and vector payload should always colocate.

hypotheses.claim: UnifiedQueryIR must preserve SET, ORDERED, MULTISET and WEIGHTED semantics across every lowerer.
hypotheses.counter: Collection kind is implementation metadata.

hypotheses.claim: Semantic equality and exact emitted representation identity must have separate receipts across process/service boundaries.
hypotheses.counter: Host-container or byte equality is an adequate semantic identity.

hypotheses.claim: A useful subset of graph, relational, FTS and vector query semantics can be differentially verified against one typed reference contract.
hypotheses.counter: Cross-model equivalence is too weakly specified for deterministic validation.

hypotheses.claim: Every query result needs an admissibility class such as authoritative exact, exact derived, approximate candidate, salience-only or model-internal.
hypotheses.counter: Provenance plus ordinary data type is sufficient.

hypotheses.claim: Cognition-critical reads require stricter source-epoch admission than exploratory associative reads.
hypotheses.counter: One global exactness policy is optimal.

hypotheses.claim: UNKNOWN dependency closure must broaden, instrument, recompute or defer rather than silently pass a narrow snapshot.
hypotheses.counter: Observed dependencies are sufficient.

hypotheses.claim: Authentic records do not establish authentic selection when mutable structure changes candidate membership.
hypotheses.counter: Record provenance is sufficient for graph-memory selection.

hypotheses.claim: Exposed selectors can be recomputed on authenticated structure with acceptable overhead for consequential operations.
hypotheses.counter: Selector replay is too expensive or too restrictive.

hypotheses.claim: One authoritative event/effect commit domain plus a durable idempotent derivation log can recover heterogeneous derived views after duplicate, reorder and loss faults.
hypotheses.counter: Direct multi-store writes are equally recoverable.

hypotheses.claim: Physical monolith remains preferable for data that genuinely requires one atomic transaction, while non-authoritative sidecars can remain outside that transaction domain.
hypotheses.counter: All data should share or avoid one transaction domain uniformly.

hypotheses.claim: Derivation-program version and source epoch are part of replay identity.
hypotheses.counter: Event history alone determines a projection uniquely.

hypotheses.claim: Activation and Assembly state should remain non-authoritative derived state keyed to canonical epochs and utility receipts.
hypotheses.counter: Canonicalizing activation simplifies cognition without safety cost.

hypotheses.claim: Utility feedback may adapt salience, decay, inhibition and routing but not silently fact truth, provenance or capability scope.
hypotheses.counter: Joint truth-and-salience adaptation is safe and more useful.

hypotheses.claim: System WorkspaceEpisode and model-internal workspace uptake should persist as separate causal receipts.
hypotheses.counter: One workspace receipt suffices.

hypotheses.claim: Linux and Android can share the same UnifiedDB semantics while using different physical placements and engines.
hypotheses.counter: Semantic equivalence requires identical storage technology.

hypotheses.claim: Physical placement should remain a reversible workload-evidence decision rather than become a semantic schema fact.
hypotheses.counter: Once consolidated, semantic contracts may safely depend on the chosen engine.
